body:
TRUST-ROOT. The context-handoff deny set is the only thing standing between a context-rotted agent and continued work. It is stored at `.adlc/handoffs/denies/<session_id>.json` with a `.adlc/.deny-store` sentinel (`packages/context-handoff/lib/deny-marker.mjs`) — inside the repository, in a tree the gated agent's own Bash tool can write to and delete. The gate's durable state is therefore writable by the party the gate exists to constrain.

Raised during the slice-5 review (PR #477) alongside the resolver trust-root defect. It is NOT introduced by that PR — it is the slice-3 storage design — so it was left out of that ticket's scope and filed here. The resolver half is T-01KZPRW2TBKCV66AZ00KYV6603; the two are independent and closing either does not close the other.

**Sequencing:** slice 5 (PR #477) adds three more adapters reading this same store. Start after it merges so the fix covers all four harnesses at once. (No graph edge: an edge would have to be added to the existing slice-5 ticket, which the rail-freeze gate forbids.)

=== THE PROBLEM ===

One root cause, two faces. Both are consequences of the store being agent-writable project state, and a fix for one does not fix the other.

1. **Subprocess D1 loss.** The hook-style harnesses (Claude Code, Codex) run a fresh process per tool call and hard-code `denyEverWritten: false` into `evaluateHandoffPreToolUse` — a fresh process cannot carry the in-memory fact that this session already denied. D1 stickiness is therefore carried entirely by what `ensureDenyMarker` managed to put on disk. If that write fails (read-only tree, full disk, a racing delete, EACCES), nothing durable is written, and the next call — arriving with a signal that has since cooled below the band — sees a cold store and ALLOWS. The in-process adapters (OpenCode, Pi) do carry the flag, so the exposure is asymmetric across harnesses, which is itself a defect: the same session on two harnesses gets two different answers.

2. **The shell can erase the store.** Shell commands are only blocked when D1-D3 has already decided to deny. Once another session consumes a record, a fresh session's shell runs ungated, and `rm -rf .adlc/handoffs .adlc/.deny-store` erases the durable identity. Slice 5 added a literal-path guard (`shellPathCandidates` + `classifyHandoffPath` in `packages/context-handoff/lib/adapter.mjs`) that denies those paths regardless of deny state, including directory prefixes and symlink aliases. It is a real narrowing and it is genuinely defeated by one indirection, because the scanner reads literal tokens out of the command string:

    d=.adlc; rm -rf "$d/handoffs"

That is not a hole to be patched by a better regex. Shell is a language; any lexical scanner over it loses. **There is no CI backstop:** `.adlc/*` is gitignored, so the deletion never reaches a diff and rails-guard never sees it.

=== WHY THE CURRENT LOCATION EXISTS ===

Do not simply move the store without answering what the repo-relative path was buying. It is per-repo (two checkouts of two projects must not share a deny set), it survives a plugin reinstall, it is inspectable by an operator debugging a stuck session, and it needs no host-specific configuration to work on a fresh clone. Any replacement must keep those properties, and must work on Linux, macOS, and Windows — the ticket-store platform matrix already runs all three.

=== REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR ===

1. The authoritative deny state MUST live where the gated agent's tools cannot reach it: host-owned storage outside the repository working tree (keyed by repo identity so it stays per-repo), or an equivalent arrangement where erasure by the agent is not possible. State which mechanism was chosen and why in the module header.
2. Erasing or corrupting anything the agent CAN still reach MUST NOT produce an allow. If the authoritative store is unreadable, the gate fails closed with a distinct reason — the existing cold-store fail-OPEN behaviour is preserved only for a store that has genuinely never been written (an adapter installed on a clean repo must not brick it), and that distinction must be decided from host-owned state, not from a file the agent can delete.
3. D1 stickiness MUST NOT depend on a successful project-tree write. A hook subprocess that cannot persist must deny rather than allow, and must reach the same verdict as an in-process adapter given the same session and signals.
4. All four harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi) read and write the relocated store through the shared adapter core — no per-harness storage divergence.
5. Existing deny records at the old location are migrated or honoured; an in-flight session must not silently lose an open deny on upgrade.
6. The binding spec is updated to describe the new location and to state the trust boundary explicitly (which party can write which artifact). The repo-relative literal-path shell guard stays as defence in depth and is documented as such, not as the control.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Deleting the entire agent-reachable handoff tree does not clear an open deny: the session still denies afterwards. verify: `node --test packages/context-handoff/test/deny-store-trust.test.mjs`
- The same holds when the deletion is expressed so the literal-path scanner cannot see it (shell variable indirection), proving the fix does not rest on the lexical guard. verify: `node --test packages/context-handoff/test/deny-store-trust.test.mjs`
- An authoritative store that exists but cannot be read fails closed with a distinct reason, while a store that has never been written on a clean repo still allows. verify: `node --test packages/context-handoff/test/deny-store-trust.test.mjs`
- A hook subprocess whose project-tree write fails still denies on the next call with a cooled signal — no `denyEverWritten: false` allow. verify: `node --test packages/context-handoff/test/deny-store-trust.test.mjs`
- A hook-style harness and an in-process harness reach the same verdict for the same session and signals. verify: `node --test packages/context-handoff/adapter-test/adapter-core.test.mjs`
- Each trust test proves it bites: with the relocation reverted the erasure DOES clear the deny, asserted against a fixture rather than by inspection. verify: `node --test packages/context-handoff/test/deny-store-trust.test.mjs`
- An open deny written at the old location before upgrade is still honoured after it. verify: `node --test packages/context-handoff/test/deny-store-trust.test.mjs`
- All four harness deny contracts pass against the relocated store. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs plugins/adlc-opencode/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs plugins/adlc-pi/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs`
- Package-level D1-D3, CLI, and adapter contracts still green. verify: `node --test packages/context-handoff/test/*.test.mjs packages/context-handoff/cli-test/*.test.mjs packages/context-handoff/adapter-test/*.test.mjs`
- The host-owned location resolves on win32 as well as on posix, asserted against a stubbed platform rather than only on the runner it happens to execute on. verify: `node --test packages/context-handoff/test/deny-store-trust.test.mjs`
- The spec names the new location and states which party can write which artifact. verify: `rg -q 'trust boundary' docs/specs/context-rot-handoff.md .adlc/specs/context-rot-handoff.md`
- The three CI gates pass on a freshly fetched base. verify: `npm run preflight`
- Trust-root tier: a distinct-provider cross-model approve is recorded before merge. verify: `node packages/prosecute/bin/adlc-prosecute.mjs tier-check --base origin/main --author-provider anthropic`

allow-suppression: none

=== WHY THIS TICKET DECLARES NO RAILS ===

Deliberate, not an oversight. Every file that would otherwise be the obvious rail pins the storage LOCATION this ticket exists to change: `docs/specs/context-rot-handoff.md` names `.adlc/handoffs/denies/<session_id>.json` and `.adlc/.deny-store` outright, `packages/context-handoff/test/deny-marker.test.mjs` and `packages/context-handoff/cli-test/cli-write.test.mjs` build fixtures at those paths, and `plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs` hard-codes them throughout. Freezing any of them would forbid the fix — the failure mode #480 was reverted for, in its other form. The invariants that must not regress are stated as acceptance criteria above and are enforced by the harness deny contracts, which must pass unmodified except where a criterion above requires the path to change. Add rails once the new location exists and there is a location-agnostic contract to freeze.

Out of scope: the resolver trust-root defect (T-01KZPRW2TBKCV66AZ00KYV6603) — separate root cause, separate fix; changing D1-D3 semantics, band thresholds, or any deny-set decision logic — this is a storage-location and durability change only; the advisory/manual tier adapters (slice 6) and Proven CI (slice 7).
title: context-handoff: deny state must not live in storage the agent's own shell can erase
